items.title: State affiliations
items.text: Slavery was central to secession. This late-1861 affiliation map uses modern state outlines; it does not map occupation or unanimity. West Virginia is omitted because it was then part of Virginia.

items.title: Fort Sumter
items.text: Confederate forces opened fire on Fort Sumter on 12 April 1861. Charleston Harbour locates the attack that began the war; the point does not describe the later Union blockade.

items.title: Missouri / St Louis
items.text: Delaware, Maryland, Kentucky and Missouri retained slavery while remaining in the Union. Rival loyalties and fighting inside these states make a simple North–South colour divide misleading.

items.title: Washington
items.text: The Emancipation Proclamation of 1863 applied to areas in rebellion, with specified exemptions. It did not itself abolish slavery everywhere in the United States; Washington locates the issuing government.

items.title: Appomattox
items.text: Lee surrendered the Army of Northern Virginia at Appomattox on 9 April 1865. The surrender was a major endpoint, but other Confederate armies surrendered later.
